notes.title: ANNOUNCEMENT! v1.4.11: THE RAD ACHIEVEMENT UPDATE IS LIVE ON STEAM
notes.content:
Hey Grifters...

[b]PATCH NOTES 1.4.11[/b]
[list]
[*] Added NEW ACHIEVEMENTS
[*] General fixes to animation issues.
[*] Fixing an issue on Switch where compression was turned off in Las Venganza
[*] Fixing an issue where players can get zoomed in by accident at the beginning of Las Venganza
[*] Changing save points in Las Venganza to not save during cutscene

[b]ANNOUNCEMENT! v1.4.11: THE RAD ACHIEVEMENT UPDATE IS LIVE ON STEAM[/b]

What’s up folks, been a minute since we added fresh patch notes, but here we are!

We’ve got some new, fresh achievements coming in. Requested by our dope Xbox community to get us to round out the GamerScore, you know we gotta bring em to Steam too. There’s a fun one in Lisbon for you, and some high score challenges in Rad Skater too, for the extreme score hunters, or the folks that know how to magically cheat at the game. ;)

In addition to that, we fixed some issues around the save point at the beginning of LV1, as players can get stuck in a weird hellish limbo state if the save happens before that cutscene is done. Well, NO LONGER. 

More fun fixes in the future, and thanks for your love and support!


Con and on, 
Dave

notes.title: For Those Using Older Saved Games (from before Dec. 14th)
notes.content:
Hey Everyone! 👋

If you are a new player and picked up The Big Con during the Steam Winter Sale, thanks a ton! ❤️

This post is specifically about a [i]potential[/i] bug for people who may have picked it up earlier, and are loading save data from before [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1139280/view/3146324738913947213]Patch v1.1.24[/url] (launched Tuesday December 14th, 2021).

We've had a small (but still concerning) number of reports from some folks who had game saves from prior to our last update, where they are hitting crashes when opening the notebook, inventory or menu. We are aware of this bug and have been troubleshooting around it; and we are happy to say that we think it has wriggled close enough to the surface for us to figure out what is causing it... right before we shut down for the holidays. It is a [i]DEEP[/i] bug, a very [i]NASTY[/i] bug, but we are on it!

We want to get this tested, up and running to you as soon as possible, but we've also encouraged our team to take time to be with family and recharge over the next two weeks. Additionally, we wouldn't want to rush a patch out to you that we haven't had the time to fully test -- which we know you'll understand. 

This bug does not seem to be affecting people with new saves in our reproductions. But, if you had a save from before the patch and go back to it now, there is a small chance you may hit this issue. We also don't want to encourage you to wipe your game, especially when we feel so close to a fix being ready. 

So for now, we wanted to fully communicate to you what we know, and promise you it’s at the top of our list to deliver when we return to the office in the first week of January. We really appreciate your understanding, and look forward to making sure this is taken care of on our return!

We couldn’t have had the amazing year we did without you, so we just want to say thanks so much. If you celebrate the upcoming holidays, then from our family to yours we wish you a safe and Happy Holiday and a Happy New Year!

- The Mighty Yell Team 🤟

notes.title: PATCH v1.1.24 aka THE CHUCKLES & CHECKPOINTS UPDATE IS LIVE
notes.content:
Hey Grifters… 

[b]PATCH NOTES v1.1.24[/b] aka THE CHUCKLES & CHECKPOINTS UPDATE
[list]
[*] Fixing an issue in Control Remapping where the player could assign two conflicting maps to the same button
[*] Minor content stability fixes and typo fixes
[*] Performance spike fixes across game through optimization
[*] Implemented fixed autosave points at each major storybeat
[*] Implemented approximately 80x more laughtrack lines.
[/list]
You’ll Laugh… You’ll Cry… You’ll… save your game more frequently! 😎

This patch is one we had to bump to a bit after launch, but we’ve locked in and stabilized our autosave points throughout the game. Major storybeats and quest completion now have your back, saving and making sure that you don’t have to worry about it (just watch the floppy disk!)

Also, we’ve added a ton more laughs, boos, and cheers to the game with our laughtrack feature. We always wanted to get more giggles into the game, and this was a great way to end off our year of patches. 

Does this mean I can say the game is now 80x funnier? 🤔

Yes. Yes it does. 😎

Happy laughing, 
- Dave at Mighty Yell

notes.title: PATCH v1.1.17 IS LIVE!
notes.content:
[b]PATCH NOTES 1.1.17 - SO MANY UPDATES! [/b]

[list]
[*] Control remapping has been added. Now players can remap buttons to any other buttons of their choice.
[*] Windowed mode has been added for PC Players.
[*] We have fixed a variety of bugs associated with control remapping and controller glyphs.
[*] We have addressed numerous level stability issues.
[*] We have made Sammy slightly easier to find in LV2. 
[*] And of course, we added a great deal of love ❤️ 
[/list]

Hey Grifters, this is a big one we’ve been working on for a while! 
You [i]might[/i] even say this patch is the motherlode… (hi Mom!) 

We are VERY excited to introduce this huge patch for you, our dedicated and amazing players. It features two huge items we’ve wanted to include since launch: [b]Windowed Mode[/b] and [b]CONTROL REMAPPING[/b].

That’s right, you can now remap all your actions as you see fit, so if you have alternate control schemes you’d prefer or want to try out, we’ve got you covered! (And if we missed something, you know we want to hear from you.)

Also, for our players using wider screens, or players that like to play with on-screen keyboards, we’ve introduced windowed mode; now you don’t have to play The Big Con in full screen mode!

In addition to these two items, we’ve introduced a TON of fixes. We’ve made some important characters easier to find, and others less likely to do weird stuff; so all in all, we are feeling good about this patch.

We’ve still got much more planned for you, so stay tuned for more updates, join our Discord or our Steam Community, and please share what you think!


Thanks for all your support & stay Rad, 

Dave 😎

notes.title: The Big Con review: a rags to riches coming of age tale
notes.content:
If Hypnospace Outlaw was the perfect distillation of 90s internet culture, then Mighty Yell's debut game The Big Con is a similarly concentrated dose of 90s pop culture. Pastel swirls, bum bags and rad catch phrases abound in this coming of age thrift adventure, in which teenager Ali must loot her way across America to save her mum's video rental store from debt collectors. With just a fistful of dollars to her name at the start of her four-odd hour road trip, Ali will need to bag 97,000 of them by the end of it to come home victorious, and she'll do it via that most tried and tested of video game tropes: the swing meter mini-game.

Read more

notes.title: THE BIG LAUNCH!!
notes.content:
Sup? The Big Con, the ‘90s adventure game where you can do crimes and stuff, is like, totally out TODAY. Finally, you can ditch your old life to scam and pickpocket your way across the country. You’re not a bad dude, and in fact, you’re not playing as a dude at all. As if!

Ali is a rad teen con artist trying to save her mom’s video store from unscrupulous loan sharks any way she can. And well, the best way is to live out a life of petty theft, sneaking around, and other silly mischief. Run around the mall, cop sweet ‘90s collectibles, and avoid people who would dare to harsh your mellow.

Peep our sweet LAUNCH TRAILER for a glimpse into the fly colors, sick soundtrack, and hella fun gameplay you can expect from The Big Con. And from all of us at Mighty Yell and Skybound Games, happy scammin’!

notes.title: Eight narrative games revealed new trailers at the Tribeca Film Festival
notes.content:
The Tribeca Film Festival has nothing to do with E3, aside from the fact that it's going on right now. Oh, and they invited eight upcoming narrative-focused games to be involved this year for their first game award category. Several of the bunch, Sable, Harold Halibut, Kena: Bridge Of Spirits, and more are games we're quite looking forward to around these parts. notes.title: Save mom's video store by doing 90s teen crimes in The Big Con this summer
notes.content:
Summer's approaching, so it's time to figure out what kind of wacky character development you're going to have during the scorching months. If you hadn't come up with a plan yet, you can always go with one of the classics: going on a cross-country road trip with a con man to somehow save your mom's video store from mobsters. That's what local sarcastic 90s teen Ali is doing in The Big Con this summer, anyhow. I hope she makes some lasting memories, because I've got bad news for her about the eventual longevity of her mom's VHS store.
